title: 1-hour onramp: integrate, measure, iterate — dev playbook
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a lightweight playbook for marketing and product to run a small set of quick experiments around a developer-first onramp for the Hosted API. Target audience: backend/frontend devs, ML engineers, platform teams who want to wire up a simple generation or embedding call in under an hour and see cost/latency signals.

TL;DR (one line):
Make it trivial to get a working inference call, measure concrete economics (latency/cost), and propose one sensible next step (pin model, add caching, or reserve capacity).

What we want to test (hypotheses):
- H1: If a dev can get a response in <10 minutes with sample code that runs locally, they are 3x more likely to try a 2nd integration.
- H2: Calling out concrete unit economics (est. $/1k tokens and p95 latency) in the quickstart increases trial-to-pay conversion.
- H3: Offering a small ‘auto-suggest’ batch config and a pre-baked cache policy will reduce perceived integration risk for production usage.

Core developer-first value props (short bullets for UX/copy experiments):
- "Start building in minutes: single-file example and working curl request — no account setup required for sandbox."
- "Predictable performance: median and p95 latency benchmarks for common request shapes."
- "Control costs from day one: sample batching and cache settings with estimated $/1k tokens."
- "Same API whether you run Hosted, Dedicated, or Private — switch without code changes."

1-hour onramp flow (practical steps for docs/marketing):
- 0–5 min: sign up -> auto-provision sandbox key (30 min TTL). Landing CTA: "Run the curl below".
- 5–15 min: curl + Node/Go snippet to call /v1/generate with a 64-token prompt. Show raw response and stream example.
- 15–30 min: run an embedding example and a tiny rerank (two-line Python). Show how to measure token usage and cost estimate.
- 30–45 min: small checklist: add error handler, inspect p95 latency via console quicklink, enable prefix caching toggle.
- 45–60 min: decision point UI in doc: "Go To Production" (reserve capacity vs PAYG). Outline expected tradeoffs in one-line bullets.

Concrete copy snippets to A/B test (homepage, quickstart, email):
- Headline A: "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and transparent economics"
- Headline B: "From prototype to SLA-backed inference — same API, better economics"
- Quickstart CTA A: "Run a request in 60 seconds"
- Quickstart CTA B: "See your first inference — no credit card"
- Pricing lead: "Pay-as-you-go with meterable token pricing (+ optional reserved capacity for predictable throughput). Typical dev apps start on PAYG; enterprise teams reserve capacity."

Pricing-language experiments (three draft variants):
- Variant 1 (dev-friendly): "Pay per token. Free 2M tokens on sign-up. Usage dashboard shows token count, latency percentiles, and cost breakdown per model."
- Variant 2 (commit tease): "Start PAYG; once sustained usage exceeds X tokens/day we recommend a Dedicated commitment with estimated savings (sample table)."
- Variant 3 (value-centred): "Tools + savings: enable our Optimize suite to get batching and cache suggestions; expect 20–50% token-cost reduction on common workloads."

Competitive notes (short, tactical):
- Cloud provider managed endpoints: they win on existing infra and IAM but lose on inference economics and model/quantization suggestions. Callout for messaging: "More predictable unit economics than raw cloud endpoints; inference-specific ops baked-in."
- LLM API providers (simplicity-first): they win on immediate simplicity. Our angle: "developer-first, but production-grade — we keep the onboarding friction low while giving ops the levers they actually need."
- Self-hosted runtimes: win on cost control at large scale, but slow to get running and maintain. Emphasize "same API across hosted and private so you can start hosted and port later."

Objections & short rebuttals (sales/enablement snippets):
- "I don’t want to lock into a provider": "You can prototype on Hosted; our API and SDKs are identical for Dedicated/Private, making migrations predictable."
- "Pay-as-you-go gets expensive": "Show real sample configs and a calculator. Also highlight Optimize recommendations and reserved capacity options."
- "Latency matters for UX": "We provide p95 latency targets, transparent benchmarks, and automatic fallbacks to lower-latency model variants when needed."

Measurement plan (what to track for the experiment):
- Time-to-first-inference (TTFI) from sign-up (goal: median < 10 min).
- Conversion to 2nd API call within 7 days.
- Activation -> Pay conversion rate.
- Dashboard engagement: how many click to 'estimate cost' or 'simulate reserve'.
- Average tokens consumed per project in first 14 days.

Quick metrics to show in the UI/docs (samples to include):
- "Estimated cost for sample prompt: ~ $0.004 / 1k tokens (example model X, 512 context)"
- "Median latency (sample hardware): 80ms; p95: 220ms (for 64-token generation)"

Experiment matrix (minimal):
- Variant A: CTA copy A + Pricing variant 1 + no free credit visible
- Variant B: CTA copy B + Pricing variant 2 + 2M free tokens banner
- Variant C: CTA copy A + Pricing variant 3 + Optimize upsell after 1st inference

Small UX details to include in implementation:
- Pre-filled prompts tailored to common dev scenarios (chat, summarization, search snippet).
- A tiny cost estimator inline (select tokens expected -> show est $/call).
- One-click toggle to enable "caching" with short explanation and expected percent cost savings.
- Console link that auto-populates telemetry (latency, token count) sent back to docs for the user to visualize.

Next steps (immediate):
- Product: add sandbox keys with 30 min TTL + sample cost estimator. (owner: Liam)
- Docs: produce "1-hour walkthrough" with curl + Node + Python snippets and the inline estimator. (owner: Priya)
- Growth: wire two email variants and a homepage placement for the A/B test. (owner: Marco)
- GT: create ticket for pricing copy + calculator and prepare success metrics dashboard. (jira:GT-4129)

Notes / fragments (brainstorm - keep or drop):
- "Call out that model quantization recommendations exist (e.g., 4-bit) — useful for cost-sensitive apps."
- "Add a ‘cost impact’ badge next to each code example showing rough $/call."
- "Try an integration checklist for Platform teams: network tests, KMS checklist, compliance quick-links."

Links referenced (placeholders):
- Confluence: INF-quickstart-ideas (brainstorm)
- Jira: GT-4129 (experiment ticket)
- GitHub: repo/PR#244 (quickstart snippets branch)
- Slack: #launchpad-quickstart (discussion thread)

Open questions to resolve before launch:
- What is the free token allowance and is it global or per-region?
- Which model variants do we show as defaults in the estimator? (balanced vs low-latency)
- Should we show committed savings estimates on the PSA landing or only post-activation?

End of doc.

(Informal notes saved — iterate quickly and pick an MVP variant to implement in the next 2 weeks.)
